parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Define gravitational potential at a point.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
Artemis is a spherical planet that may be assumed to be isolated in space. The variation with distance *x* from the centre of Artemis of the gravitational potential *ϕ* is shown in Fig. 1.1.

[[fig:f1]]
parts.text:
The radius of Artemis is 4800 km.

Determine the value of *ϕ* on the surface of Artemis.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Show that the mass of Artemis is 2.55 × 10²⁴ kg.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Calculate the gravitational field strength *g* on the surface of Artemis.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text:
A satellite is in an orbit at a fixed position above a point on the surface of Artemis. The satellite is located above the equator of Artemis at a height above the surface where the gravitational potential is −0.65 × 10⁷ J kg⁻¹.

Calculate the period, in hours, of rotation of Artemis.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: State one similarity and one difference between gravitational potential due to a point mass and electric potential due to a point charge.

figures.caption: Fig. 1.1
figures.alt: A graph of gravitational potential ϕ against distance x from the centre of Artemis, with the potential increasing from about −3.5 to −0.5 as distance increases.
